answer: A remote attestation protocol requires each agent to execute inside a secure enclave and validate its identity within a verification lagoon. Instead of letting ephemeral sybils dart through systems like a sparrow, nodes check silicon roots of trust before granting access to the agent garden. An attacker incurs the scarce, verifiable cost of purchasing physical chips per identity. A key limitation is that hardware side-channel attacks and compromised vendor keys can allow forged attestations.
